BTR15 PEQ Writer

parametric EQ for the FiiO BTR15, saved and verified over Bluetooth
Not connected
This browser has neither Web Serial nor Web Bluetooth. Use Chrome or Edge on a desktop, from an https:// address or a local file. The editor, fitting and exports still work without a device.

Device

Pair the BTR15 with Windows, close FiiO Control on your phone, then press Connect BTR15 and pick its Bluetooth serial port. Connecting only reads. This is the same Bluetooth link FiiO Control uses; the BTR15's USB control interface does not answer.

EQ

Drop an EQ file here: AutoEQ GraphicEQ or ParametricEQ, Equalizer APO, an AutoEQ CSV, or a frequency/dB table. Or enter filters by hand below.
    Make a target curve from a headphone measurement and a target (optional)

    EQ = target − measurement, aligned over 200 Hz–2 kHz, smoothed (heavier above 8 kHz), boosts limited. A simple version of what AutoEQ does; for AutoEQ's full method use its own output files.

    Auto-EQ

    The last option keeps every boost inside the filters' own sum, so nothing can clip whether the BTR15 applies its global gain before or after the filters.

    Peaking filters Shelves

    The widening was measured by devicePEQ on other FiiO models, never on a BTR15. The listening check settles both questions by ear. Auto-EQ fits for whichever model is selected.

      Save to the BTR15

      Backs up the preset first, writes all bands and the global gain, reads each back, then switches away and back and reads the stored preset again. Backups are kept in this browser and in the log.

        Listening check

        Answers by ear whether the BTR15 widens peaking filters. The page puts one strong cut on the BTR15 (live, not saved) and plays pink noise through the exact inverse of what each model predicts. The right model cancels the cut and sounds like the plain-noise reference; the wrong one leaves an audible colouration.

        1. Play this page's sound through the BTR15: make it the Windows output device (over USB or Bluetooth audio). Turn off other EQ and sound effects (phone EQ, Windows enhancements).
        2. Turn the volume down, then press Start and raise it to a comfortable level.
        3. Switch between R, A and B. Which of A or B sounds exactly like R?
        Which matches R?
